body.heading: The wide-awake bed problem
paragraphs: If you spend long stretches lying in bed awake and annoyed, your brain starts linking the bed itself with being alert and frustrated — the opposite of what you want. Sleep guidance commonly suggests breaking that link.

The classic advice: if you have been awake for roughly twenty minutes and feel nowhere near sleep, get up. Go somewhere dim and do something dull — a boring book, quiet tidying — until sleepiness returns, then go back to bed.

body.heading: Lower the stakes of tonight
paragraphs: One short night is unpleasant but not a disaster; most people function better the next day than their 2 a.m. predictions suggest. Treating tonight's sleep as a test you must pass adds exactly the pressure that keeps you awake.

If sleeplessness becomes your normal pattern for several weeks, or tiredness is affecting school, work or safety, please see a health professional. Persistent sleep problems are common, treatable, and worth proper attention.

takeaway: If sleep won't come, get up gently — and lower the pressure on tonight.
